title: Bee-eater vs dragonfly

scenes.headline: Caught in mid-air. Now the hard part.
Whack it on the branch
scenes.body: Bee-eaters catch big flying insects, then strike them against a perch before swallowing.

scenes.headline: Bees get extra handling
scenes.body: With stinging prey, it sometimes rubs the tail end on a branch to squeeze the venom out.
scenes.source: Birds of the World, Cornell Lab

scenes.headline: Dragonflies are aerial predators too
scenes.body: They catch other insects in flight — this one met a faster hunter.

caption:
The bee-eater's rule: never swallow it while it can still fight back.

Bee-eaters are sit-and-wait hunters: they watch from a bare twig or wire, sally out to grab a flying insect, and bring it back to the perch to deal with it.

Source: Birds of the World (Cornell Lab), European Bee-eater; Combes et al. 2012, J. Exp. Biol.. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Small-scale predation (bird vs insect) that teaches a real technique without gore. HIGH-RISK format with third-party footage; the series needs our own clips (bee-eaters on Bengaluru wires are easy to film).
